This testing was conducted in heating mode, and its goals were to assess the UUT’s capability to complete the following: o Reduce its heating capacity, using native controls, to the lowest level when the outdoor temperature is 47oF. o Maintain heating performance when the outdoor temperature is 5oF and -10oF o Manage defrosting operation to minimize peak power demand. o Transition smoothly between zone set point temperatures of 70oF and 75oF and prioritize mechanical heating when the outdoor temperature is 17oF. o Allow backup heat to work in parallel with mechanical heating to meet the building load when the outdoor temperature is 5oF. 2.4 RESULTS Both prototypes successfully met all requirements of the Test Plan. Therefore, Carrier Corporation has met the lab test requirements of the Commercial Building HVAC Technical Challenge. 7 3. SUBJECT INVENTIONS This CRADA did not result in any subject inventions. This was not unexpected, as noted in Clause 3 of the Technical Assistance Agreement (TAA) between Carrier Corporation and UT-Battelle, LLC that notes the Participant (Carrier) and Contractor (UT-Battelle) do not intend for the agreement to result in intellectual property. 4. COMMERCIALIZATION POSSIBILITIES The results of the CRADA testing support that the Carrier commercial rooftop systems designated for the Challenge meet the requirements of the Challenge. Based on the performance of one sample of each capacity, the products appear to be strong candidates for commercialization. 5. PLANS FOR FUTURE COLLABORATION Coincident with testing the Carrier commercial rooftop systems for the Challenge, ORNL researchers welcomed meeting with Carrier personnel. Their strong engineering abilities were evident during interactions before and during the short testing period. ONRL would welcome and will actively seek further collaboration with Carrier on other projects. 6. CONCLUSIONS The purpose of this CRADA was to test a nominal 10-ton capacity and a nominal 15-ton capacity rooftop commercial heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system supplied by Carrier Corporation to determine if they met the laboratory test requirements of the United States Department of Energy Commercial Building HVAC Technology Challenge. Results of the laboratory testing completed at ORNL demonstrated that the systems met all requirements of the Challenge. Carrier Corporation has successfully completed this aspect of the Challenge. This CRADA report briefly described the Challenge, the test plan created to measure the success of heat pump systems provided by Challenge participants, and the results of laboratory testing of the Carrier commercial rooftop systems. 7.
